title: ksp.query
description: Bulk read with one selector instead of many calls (04 §2): vessels (active, loaded, handles, nameLike, type), optional parts and modules (type), and the fields to read. Vessel fields: name, handle, type, situation, body, lat, lon, altitude, heightFromTerrain, srfSpeed, obtSpeed, verticalSpeed, horizontalSrfSpeed, heading, pitch, roll, course, mach, geeForce, dynamicPressurekPa, staticPressurekPa, atmDensity, externalTemperature, mass, missionTime, partCount, crewCount, currentStage, loaded, packed, landed, splashed, isActive, controllable, ctrlState.mainThrottle, ctrlState.pitch, ctrlState.yaw, ctrlState.roll, ctrlState.wheelThrottle, ctrlState.wheelSteer, actionGroups.sas, actionGroups.rcs, actionGroups.gear, actionGroups.brakes, actionGroups.lights. Module fields are the module's KSPField names (see ksp.module.describe). aggregate: perVessel (one row per vessel; module fields reduced with `reduce`), perModule or perPart.

select.description: Selector (04 §2): vessels, optional parts and modules.

vessels.description: Which vessels. All conditions must match; omit to select every loaded vessel.

loaded.description: only loaded vessels (true) or only unloaded ones (false)

nameLike.description: glob on the vessel name, e.g. "DDG*"

type.description: KSP vessel types, e.g. Ship, Plane, Probe

parts.description: Which parts (only when modules or part fields are wanted).

nameLike.description: glob on the part name (config name)

modules.description: Which part modules. Fields are then read from each module (Tier 0 KSPFields).

type.description: module class names, e.g. ModuleHullBreach, MissileFire

fields.description: Fields to read. Vessel fields (altitude, srfSpeed, ctrlState.mainThrottle, ... see ksp.query description) or module KSPField names when modules are selected; prefix with "vessel." to read a vessel field per module row.

reduce.description: how perVessel combines several modules' numeric values

cursor.description: opaque cursor from a previous result's "cursor" to get the next page

format.description: "compact" = a few readable text lines (best for LLMs), "json" = structured
